newsitem.title: USA: Russian economy encouraging, challenges ahead - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Russian economy encouraging, challenges ahead - Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Saturday there appeared to be signs of progress in the Russian economy, although the new reform team of First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais still faced challenges.
Inflation was better and Russia's once shaky relations with the International Monetary Fund were in good shape, he told a news conference at the Group of Seven summit in Denver.
"I think it is an encouraging picture," Rubin said. "Obviously there are major challenges they have got to deal with...but I think there are signs of real progress."
He said Russia's $2 billion eurobond had been issued on what he considered "remarkably favourable" terms.
The eurobond, launched earlier this week, was Russia's third issue as a sovereign borrower and the largest by a transitional economy -- a country moving from communism to capitalism.
Reform chief Chubais told a news conference earlier that Russia would have been able to get as much as $4 billion, but that it had only sought $2 billion.
Rubin, speaking after meeting Chubais, defended the summit decision to hold financial discussions without Russia.
"There are financial and economic issues in which the Western industrialised countries are in a different position to what Russia is now," he said.

"It is more fruitful to have discussions amongst those who share that commonality and that's why the finance ministers met as a G7," he added, noting that Russia was still a borrower from the IMF and World Bank.
The G7 comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin has participated in most of the sessions of the Denver summit, officially called The Summit of the Eight.
